candidate.title: IN-Seq/Tn-Seq
candidate.scope: Grouped Illumina schematic of the MmeI-based junction-tag architecture targeted as insertion sequencing (INSeq; IN-Seq in the card title) and transposon sequencing (Tn-Seq). The extracted route begins with genomic DNA already containing a transposon with MmeI-adapted terminal inverted repeats, continues through digestion and adapter ligation, and ends with the combined PCR/sequencing block and insertion-site readout. The two primary implementations support this shared schematic route with explicitly qualified genomic-tag lengths; grouping does not establish aliases, interchangeable complete protocols, or applicability to all Tn-seq variants. The left generic transposon icon is introductory, and the two end cuts are parts of one depicted route.

states.label: Bacterial genomic DNA containing an MmeI-adapted transposon insertion
features: The far-left transposon icon introduces the assay; the expanded substrate labels an inverted MmeI recognition site at the left transposon end and an MmeI recognition site at the right end.

The chemical substrate is DNA from a transposon-mutant bacterial population. The biological target is the location and relative representation of the insertion mutants, carried by transposon–genome junctions.

At this schematic boundary the transposon is already integrated. INSeq is supported by pSAM with MmeI-modified mariner inverted repeats; the cited Tn-Seq implementation uses magellan6 with recognition sites in its inverted repeats.

states.label: MmeI-released transposon-containing DNA with short adjacent genomic flanks
features: The two outward cuts delimit the same insertion-bearing fragment. The retained central segment and short genomic flanks continue into the adapter panel; the drawing does not establish separate processing branches.

The diagram annotates both cleavage spans 20bp. For INSeq, the primary paper explicitly reports two 16-bp genomic sequences outside the transposon; the cited Tn-Seq paper describes a 20-bp bacterial sequence in the eventual library. These are member-specific tag descriptions, not a uniform 20-bp genomic-flank assertion for the grouped card.
Physical linkage between a transposon end and adjacent bacterial DNA retains the insertion-site identity while most surrounding genomic sequence is excluded from the retained library substrate.

states.label: Adapter-ligated insertion-associated DNA library templates
features: Colored adapter segments flank the retained internal fragment in the schematic.

The library carries transposon-adjacent genomic sequence together with terminal library interfaces. The flanking genomic sequence identifies the insertion; adapter sequences provide downstream amplification/sequencing interfaces.

For INSeq, the reported amplification interface is a transposon-specific primer paired with an adapter-specific primer. The Tn-Seq paper describes bacterial sequence flanked by Illumina-specific sequences in the amplified product.

states.label: Sequenced genomic tags identifying transposon insertion sites
features: The rightmost output is labeled Transposon insertion sites. The two short horizontal marks do not by themselves specify a sequencing-read orientation or platform read mode.

Short genomic sequences adjacent to the transposon can be assigned to a reference genome to identify insertion locations when placement is unambiguous. INSeq reports pairing information from either side of an insertion; Tn-Seq reports mapping and counting its 20-bp genomic reads.

Read counts represent the relative abundance of insertion mutants in the sampled population. Fitness or quantitative genetic interaction requires suitable comparisons between populations or genetic backgrounds; the drawing ends at insertion-site readout.

operations.label: MmeI digestion
operations.description: MmeI recognizes the sites engineered into opposite transposon ends and cleaves adjacent DNA outside those ends. The input is genomic DNA with an integrated transposon; the retained output is a transposon-containing fragment with short flanking genomic tags. The two enzyme drawings describe the two ends of this local digestion instance.
operations.mechanism: The INSeq paper identifies MmeI as a Type IIs restriction enzyme. The recognition sites orient cleavage outward into flanking genomic DNA. The drawing labels the spans 20bp; the INSeq-specific interpretation retains its paper-reported 16-bp genomic flanks. MmeI is the enzyme acting on the substrate, not a DNA product.
operations.information_effect: Enriches an insertion-associated DNA representation: each retained short genomic flank remains linked to a transposon end, enabling the insertion locus to be inferred after sequencing.

operations.label: PCR and sequence
operations.description: Amplifies the adapter-bearing insertion-associated templates and sequences their short genomic tags. The diagram combines these actions in one block and labels the output Transposon insertion sites. Primary papers clarify how genomic-tag sequences can be mapped to establish those sites.
operations.mechanism: INSeq reports amplification with a transposon-specific and an adapter-specific primer followed by Illumina sequencing. Tn-Seq reports an amplified product containing a 20-bp bacterial sequence flanked by Illumina-specific sequences. Reference assignment explains the depicted output and is not expanded into a separate unshown analysis workflow.
operations.information_effect: Converts physical transposon–genome junction information into sequence tags and insertion-site identities. Counts of tags support relative mutant representation; population comparisons can connect changes in representation to fitness. This is not a readout of sequence mutations within the transposon.

method_scopes.rationale: IN-Seq in the card title and insertion sequencing (INSeq) in the image refer to INSeq as named by Goodman et al. Full-text Figure 1B and library-preparation text independently establish the depicted MmeI digestion → adapter ligation → PCR/sequencing sequence for the pSAM/mariner implementation. All three local operations therefore apply at this schematic level, with the INSeq-specific 16-bp genomic-flank interpretation recorded explicitly. The schematic’s prepared input already contains the integrated MmeI-adapted transposon. Unshown genomic-DNA preparation, size selection, combinatorial pooling, and experimental selection are not additional graph operations. This shared architecture does not assert identical complete implementations for the grouped names.

method_scopes.rationale: The title and image explicitly target transposon sequencing (Tn-Seq), associated by the card with van Opijnen et al. This scope is the cited MmeI-based magellan6 implementation: its primary Figure 1 establishes recognition sites in inverted repeats, MmeI digestion, and PCR products with 20-bp bacterial DNA and Illumina interfaces. The grouped diagram and catalogue explicitly supply the intervening adapter-ligation step. Together these sources support all three operations on the depicted already integrated, MmeI-adapted substrate; they do not extend this exact route to every workflow later called Tn-seq. The unshown circle method and other applications in the bibliography do not add targets or alternate branches.

corrections.primary_statement: Goodman et al. report that MmeI cleaves 16 bp outside the INSeq transposon and recovers two 16-bp adjacent genomic sequences. Van Opijnen et al. describe 20-bp bacterial sequence in the Tn-Seq product. Consequently the candidate states and operations use 16-bp genomic flanks for INSeq and retain the source-reported 20-bp Tn-Seq tag description, without treating the drawing’s two labels as proof that both implementations recover identical genomic tag lengths.
